questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Given by an Equation in Standard Form
questions.problem:
Consider the line $x=5$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $x=5$ passes through the points $A(5,0)$ and $B(5,1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(-5,0)$ and ${B}^{′}(-4,1).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =\frac{1-0}{-4-(-5)}(x-(-5)) \\ y & =x+5 \\ x-y+5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=2x-3$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=12.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=2x-3$ passes through the points $A(0,-3)$ and $B(1,-1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -6 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(0,-6)$ and ${B}^{′}(2,-1).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+6 & =\frac{-1+6}{2-0}(x-0) \\ y+6 & =\frac{5}{2}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+6 & =\frac{5}{2}x \\ 2y+12 & =5x \\ 5x-2y & =12\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=\frac{1}{3}x+1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=15.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=\frac{1}{3}x+1$ passes through the points $A(0,1)$ and $B(3,2)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 16 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(2,-1)$ and ${B}^{′}(16,7).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+1 & =\frac{7-(-1)}{16-2}(x-2) \\ y+1 & =\frac{8}{14}(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =\frac{4}{7}(x-2) \\ 7y+7 & =4x-8 \\ 4x-7y & =15\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=-1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=-8.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=-1$ passes through the points $P(0,-1)$ and $Q(1,-1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${P}^{′}(0,2)$ and ${Q}^{′}(4,3).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${P}^{′}$ and ${Q}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-2 & =\frac{3-2}{4-0}(x-0) \\ y-2 & =\frac{1}{4}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-8 & =x \\ x-4y & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=3$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=21.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=3$ passes through the points $P(0,3)$ and $Q(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 10 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${P}^{′}(9,3)$ and ${Q}^{′}(10,1).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${P}^{′}$ and ${Q}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =\frac{1-3}{10-9}(x-9) \\ y-3 & =-2(x-9)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-3 & =-2x+18 \\ 2x+y & =21\end{aligned}
$$
